original_query: SELECT EMP.SAL + BONUS.COMM, SUM(BONUS.SAL + BONUS.SAL + 100) OVER (PARTITION BY BONUS.JOB RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) FROM EMP INNER JOIN BONUS ON EMP.ENAME = BONUS.ENAME AND EMP.DEPTNO = 10
rewritten_query:
SELECT E.SAL + B.COMM,
       SUM(2 * B.SAL + 100) OVER (PARTITION BY B.JOB)
FROM EMP E
INNER JOIN BONUS B ON E.ENAME = B.ENAME
WHERE E.DEPTNO = 10

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Move EMP.DEPTNO = 10 from the JOIN ON clause to the WHERE clause (equivalent for inner join) for clearer filter semantics.
Simplify BONUS.SAL + BONUS.SAL + 100 to 2 * BONUS.SAL + 100, reducing redundant addition.
The explicit window frame RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING with no ORDER BY is the whole partition, so it can be omitted while keeping the same semantics.

The window sort/partition cost is minor relative to the large BONUS scan/hash join; keep the window function rather than replacing with a CTE aggregate join, since a CTE would risk materialization and double scan. Recommended supporting indexes: BONUS(ENAME) INCLUDE (JOB, SAL, COMM) and EMP(DEPTNO, ENAME) INCLUDE (SAL).
